title: La Dernière Classe
author: Alphonse Daudet
note: Alsace, 1871: France has lost the war against Prussia, and Alsace now belongs to Germany, so German becomes compulsory in its schools. A young boy, Franz, tells the story of his teacher's very last French lesson. The story often uses the passé simple, a literary past tense: when you hear "je vis" or "il dit", just think "I saw", "he said".

segments.fr: Alors il se tourna vers le tableau,
segments.en: Then he turned to the blackboard,

segments.fr: prit un morceau de craie
segments.en: took a piece of chalk

segments.fr: et, en appuyant de toutes ses forces,
segments.en: and, pressing with all his strength,

segments.fr: il écrivit aussi gros qu'il put :
segments.en: he wrote as large as he could:

segments.fr: « VIVE LA FRANCE ! »
segments.en: "LONG LIVE FRANCE!"

segments.fr: Puis il resta là, la tête appuyée au mur,
segments.en: Then he stayed there, his head leaning against the wall,

segments.fr: et, sans parler, avec sa main, il nous faisait signe :
segments.en: and, without speaking, he signalled to us with his hand:

segments.fr: « C'est fini… allez-vous-en. »
segments.en: "It's over… go away."
